strings.name: Billie Eilish
strings.summary: Billie Eilish began making recordings at home with her brother and long-term collaborator Finneas. Quiet singing, layered vocals and rhythmic experimentation became central to her style. From the online circulation of “Ocean Eyes” to albums such as When We All Fall Asleep, Where Do We Go?, she brought youthful anxiety, relationships and identity into pop songwriting. Her work also includes film themes and a concert film she co-directed.
strings.coverageNote: Sources checked through 13 November 2026; selected chronology extends to the May 2026 concert film release. Grammy wins follow the awards list; collaborators on films and songs are identified.
strings.influence.rationale: Influenced a new generation of pop songwriting through home-produced music and a distinctive voice, bringing young people's psychological experiences into popular narratives.
strings.facts.fact-01.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.fact-02.label: Long-term collaborator
strings.facts.fact-02.value: Her brother, songwriter and producer Finneas O’Connell
strings.highlights.highlight-01.title: From home recording to an international audience
strings.highlights.highlight-01.text: With Finneas, developed intimate vocals and detailed production into a musical language for albums and large live performances.
strings.highlights.highlight-02.title: Recognition for film songs
strings.highlights.highlight-02.text: Shared two original-song Oscars with Finneas for “No Time to Die” and “What Was I Made For?”
strings.timeline.event-01.title: Co-directed concert film reaches cinemas
strings.timeline.event-01.text: Co-directed Hit Me Hard and Soft: The Tour with James Cameron, bringing the tour’s performances into a 3D concert film.
strings.timeline.event-02.title: “Wildflower” wins Song of the Year
strings.timeline.event-02.text: Shared the Grammy for Song of the Year with Finneas for “Wildflower,” extending the reach of Hit Me Hard and Soft.
strings.timeline.event-03.title: Releases Hit Me Hard and Soft
strings.timeline.event-03.text: Her third studio album moved between restrained singing and more forceful passages, continuing her creative partnership with Finneas.
strings.timeline.event-04.title: Wins a second Oscar for a Barbie song
strings.timeline.event-04.text: Won original song with Finneas for “What Was I Made For?,” a song for Barbie that considers identity and purpose.
strings.timeline.event-05.title: “No Time to Die” wins an Oscar
strings.timeline.event-05.text: Shared the original-song Oscar with Finneas for the theme to the James Bond film No Time to Die.
strings.timeline.event-06.title: Releases Happier Than Ever
strings.timeline.event-06.text: Her second album explored fame, relationships and personal boundaries through varied vocal intensity and arrangements.
strings.timeline.event-07.title: Wins all four general-field Grammys
strings.timeline.event-07.text: Her debut album and “Bad Guy” earned Album, Record and Song of the Year, alongside Best New Artist.
strings.timeline.event-08.title: Releases her debut studio album
strings.timeline.event-08.text: Released When We All Fall Asleep, Where Do We Go?, developing her home-recorded sound for a wider audience.
strings.timeline.event-09.title: Releases her debut EP
strings.timeline.event-09.text: Released dont smile at me, collecting “Ocean Eyes” and other early songs and recordings.
strings.timeline.event-10.title: “Ocean Eyes” circulates online
strings.timeline.event-10.text: Recorded a song written and produced by Finneas; its online audience became a starting point for her professional career.
strings.timeline.event-11.title: Born in Los Angeles
strings.timeline.event-11.text: Grew up in an artistic family, was homeschooled and began writing and recording with her brother as a teenager.
